answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making each identity costly to forge: to join, an agent must burn ten minutes of verifiable useful work and lock a 500-POA deposit for 30 days, like a pigment fingerprint no two agents share. A forger flooding the ocean of identities with 1,000 fakes pays 1,000 times the work plus 500,000 POA locked, while honest agents pay once. Misbehavior slashes the deposit and burns the fingerprint, so fakes cost more than they can ever earn.
